data.narrative:
Curio Solutions is a Series A nuclear energy company founded by Ed McGinnis and Pete Zweifel that has raised $16M+ to date. The valuation analysis draws on a comp universe of 11 total peers—3 public (OKLO, NNE, SMR) and 8 private entities in the nuclear energy sector at same or adjacent stages, including Fuse Energy, Valar Atomics, Helion, Oklo, and X-Energy.

Two triangulation methods apply. Stage-progression analysis uses the $16M raised as a valuation proxy and applies a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical for Series A advancement, implying a $32M post-valuation. Peer-median analysis across three same-sector, same/adjacent-stage comparables yields a median valuation of $808M; the peer sample spans $200M (Fuse Energy, Series A) to $6.0B (Valar Atomics, Series B), with Nano Nuclear Energy at $808M (Seed stage).

The two methods produce a wide triangulated range of $27M to $929M, with a median of $420M. The disparity reflects stage and maturity heterogeneity within the peer set—the peer-median method anchors heavily to late-stage, well-capitalized comparables, while stage-progression applies a more conservative multiplier to observed capital. Key uncertainties include technology differentiation relative to peers, path to revenue, and capital efficiency. A defensible valuation range would center between $200M and $500M, contingent on detailed analysis of Curio's competitive positioning and near-term value inflection points.
